hometownMyth.text: The Dreaming Family: One family each generation is born with prophetic dreams, and by custom they belong to the town — dreams recorded, interpreted by the council, acted on. The family has never refused; no one is certain they could. The current dreamer is nine, hates it, and has started lying, and exactly one councilwoman has noticed that the town is now navigating by the invented dreams of a spiteful child, and is saying nothing, because the invented ones keep coming true.

hometownMyth.text: The Bone Tithe: Every seventh harvest, the miller buries one sack of flour unground at the field's edge. His grandfather skipped it once and the mill burned. Buyers accept the seventh-year shortfall without comment, the sack is carried out in silence, and the burying-spot is churned earth going back centuries — nobody has ever dug one back up, and the miller owns three dogs to keep it that way.

hometownMyth.text: The Star-Sown Field: The rare herbs in the high meadow grew from the dust of a fallen comet, and the herbs are real: they cure what they shouldn't, they grow in a perfect 300-ft ellipse, and they die if transplanted an inch beyond it. Herbalists rent harvesting rights by the hour. What the town doesn't advertise: the ellipse is measurably narrower each decade, the way a wound closes — or the way something buried finishes being spent.

hometownMyth.text: The Agreed Silence: There is one question you do not ask here — about the north road, and what happened to the last survey party. Locals say it's rude.
